evidence.ref: The failure signature and recurrence detection ship as pure functions in the engine organ .warp/incident_reconcile.py (record schema warp.reconciliation/v1, standard library only, 937 lines against the 1000-line module_lines budget, longest function reconcile_incident at 95 lines against the 120-line budget). Its ONE IMPURE EDGE is now a sibling organ, .warp/reconciliation_store.py (333 lines, longest function settle at 24), which owns the append-only compare-and-swap receipt store, the draft writes, and the draft path guard; the split was the reviewer's own judgment about a module sitting at its budget with four defects in it, and it puts the compare-and-swap and the path guard in one place. failure_signature(incident) is a deterministic normalized digest over exactly the four identity-of-failure fields (affected_behavior, signal, and affected_spec / affected_area when present), each whitespace-normalized and case-folded. recurrence(incident, prior_incidents) returns the ordered, de-duplicated ids of prior incidents sharing the signature, excluding the incident itself and skipping records whose signature cannot be computed. A non-empty recurrence set sets recurrence_of and missing_specification true on the receipt, naming the recurrence what WARP.md already calls it: a missing specification.

Selftest assertions (scripts/selftest.py): determinism; identity fields whitespace-normalized and case-folded; each of the four identity fields CHANGES the signature (4 assertions); title, severity, id and timeline each do NOT change it (4 assertions); a malformed record has no computable signature; the signature is identical ACROSS PROCESSES under two different PYTHONHASHSEED values (the purity claim proven, not asserted); a second seeded incident with the same identity fields is detected against the first; the recurrence set is ordered as recorded and de-duplicated; the incident excludes itself; a malformed prior record is skipped rather than silently matched; an unrelated failure is NOT a recurrence (control); a recurrence is named a missing specification; a settled reconciliation of a recurring failure records recurrence_of and missing_specification true. Both organs are asserted under the module budget, the pass is asserted to declare NO store, path guard or compare-and-swap of its own (it re-exports the store's by name), and the store organ is asserted stdlib-only, loading exactly one shipped owner (action.py, for the whitelist store LOCATION) and no enforcement module.

reconcile_incident fails closed on six independent conditions, each refused by name through the injected fail(name, msg) reporter: (a) a status that is not diagnosed (an already-closed incident takes the AC4 replay path, not a second settlement); (b) no human diagnosis validation supplied at all, its ABSENCE being a refusal rather than a default-allow; (c) a validation whose actor is a machine actor, the set REUSED from the shipped .warp/authorization.py MACHINE_ACTORS loaded by path exactly as .warp/request_reconcile.py loads it, so the responder can never validate its own diagnosis (NG4); (d) a validation that BINDS NO REMEDY while a remedy exists (validation_binds_no_remedy: an attestation names its subject, the shape request_reconcile's attestations already carry); (e) a bound digest that does not equal the digest the module INDEPENDENTLY RECOMPUTES from the incident record's diagnosis material AND, whenever a remedy exists, that remedy's identity plus its canonical proposal digest; (f) an open emergency backfill debt reported by an INJECTED debt_reader, dependency-inverted so no enforcement module is imported into a contracts-area organ, and standing down honestly when no reader is declared.

WHAT THE HUMAN ATTESTS TO IS WHAT THE HUMAN VALIDATED (the round-1 defect F2, closed). Round 1 recomputed the material from the incident record alone, and warp.incident/v1 has NO diagnosis field: the diagnosis and its cited evidence live on warp.remedy/v1, which validate_remedy requires precisely so a diagnosis rests on cited artifacts. The material was therefore the failure identity plus a timestamp, and the reviewer swapped the ENTIRE remedy (proposed_action rollback_deploy replaced by drop_customer_table) with the validation untouched and it still settled, rendering the runbook draft for the destructive action. diagnosis_material(incident, remedy) now binds the remedy's id and its CANONICAL PROPOSAL DIGEST, recomputed through the shipped .warp/action_executor.py proposal_digest. That binding surface is a deliberate choice over hashing a hand-picked {diagnosis, evidence, proposed_action} subset, and the module docstring carries the justification: the canonical digest covers the diagnosis, every cited artifact and the proposed action AND the remainder of the proposal's substance (rollback plan, risk class, autonomy level, reversibility analysis, required authorization), and it is the SAME digest the executor's confirmation and the two-key rule bind, so the human's validation and the executor's confirmation bind one artifact identity rather than two definitions of it. This is what makes the WARP-0619 lesson invocation earned rather than decorative: the value is recomputed here from the records, and what it now covers is the diagnosis a human actually read. The receipt's diagnosis_validation block records bound_remedy and a binds field spelling out what the digest covers, so a stranger reads the binding rather than inferring it from the block's name.

Each of the six refusals proven by name over seeded fixtures, plus a non-mapping and a no-validator variant of (b), 4 machine-actor spellings for (c), a different-remedy-id variant of (d), a stale-record digest variant of (e), and a reader-raises and a stand-down variant of (f). THE REVIEWER'S EXACT ATTACK IS A NAMED ASSERTION: the same validation with the entire remedy swapped (rollback_deploy replaced by drop_customer_table) now refuses with diagnosis_digest_mismatch, settles nothing, and writes NO draft at all - and a companion assertion proves the swapped remedy is itself contract-valid (INC.validate_remedy reports zero problems), so the refusal comes from the binding and not from a malformed record. Seven further assertions prove each of the remedy's diagnosis, evidence, proposed_action, rollback, risk_class, autonomy_level and required_authorization changes the recomputed digest. The positive control proves the pass does not over-fire: a diagnosed incident with a valid non-machine validation that names its remedy and whose bound digest matches, and no open debt, SETTLES. Structural assertions bind the architecture: the organ loads only shipped owners by path (the five contract owners, the one parser, its own store sibling) and NO enforcement module, the enforcement area appears in both organs only as prose explaining why it is not depended on (never an import, never a _load), and both organs are stdlib only and start no process, thread or timer (NG3).

A settled reconciliation writes two drafts a human promotes: a regression criteria draft (schema warp.regression_criteria/v1) rendered from the failure mode and carrying the incident id, the failure signature and the recurrence set; and a runbook action draft rendered from the remedy's proposed action, carrying review_status proposed so the shipped whitelist physics excludes it. Both are written into the store's drafts directory, .warp/incident_drafts/{criteria,runbook}/ by default. HONEST CORRECTION (round-2 review): that directory is a CONSTRUCTOR ARGUMENT, not a fixed location, and the guard is a two-root DENY-LIST rather than a containment check, so a caller supplying another drafts directory can write drafts outside it (the reviewer settled clean reconciliations writing into scripts/ and .git/hooks/). What is guaranteed is only what the deny-list names: nothing lands inside the action whitelist store or the spec corpus. THE PATH GUARD IS DECIDED ON THE RESOLVED PATH (the round-1 defect F1, closed): the store refuses by name (forbidden_draft_path) any target whose REAL absolute path falls inside the action whitelist store or the spec corpus, with every '..' collapsed, every symlink followed, relative targets anchored, and every segment compared CASE-INSENSITIVELY because this engine ships to macOS and Windows adopters whose filesystems are case insensitive; a target Path.resolve() cannot resolve at all (a symlink LOOP) is refused too, because a target that cannot be resolved cannot be cleared. HONEST CORRECTION (round-2 review): an UNREADABLE PARENT is NOT such a case on Linux and CPython, where resolve() succeeds on a mode-000 parent and the guard returns no forbidden root; the write then raises PermissionError rather than a named refusal. The shipped _real_parts docstring carries the same overclaim and is recorded for the follow-up hardening item rather than edited after review. Round 1 scanned the raw Path.parts, which let a '..' traversal, a symlinked drafts directory and the case variants .WARP/Actions/ and Specs/ through. THE STRUCTURAL VALIDITY IS ENFORCED, NOT EXHIBITED (the round-1 defect F4, closed): the RENDERED runbook draft is parsed by the ONE parser (validate.parse_yamlish, loaded by path) and judged by the ONE validator (action.validate_action) inside the write path, and a draft the shipped contract would refuse is refused by name (structurally_invalid_draft) with the contract's own message rather than written; nothing is reimplemented here. The renderer additionally refuses any review status other than proposed and refuses a review verdict field entirely. Promotion stays a human act of moving and reviewing a draft. The adopter-facing capabilities.yaml entry is updated to state exactly these properties, including the resolution, the case-insensitivity and the two new refusals.

Both drafts are written and re-render byte-identically; the runbook draft validates against the shipped warp.action/v1 contract; the shipped action_reviewed() says it is NOT reviewed; build_whitelist over the draft's OWN directory does not contain it (NG2); the regression criteria draft is rendered from the failure mode; a draft target inside the action whitelist store is refused by name; a draft target inside the spec corpus is refused by name. F1: five crafted targets are each refused by name with nothing written - a '..' traversal out of the drafts directory, a drafts directory that IS a symlink into the store, a case variant of the store path, a case variant of the spec corpus, and a target that cannot be resolved (a real symlink loop on a temporary tree) - and a further assertion proves the guard NAMES the real forbidden root behind each disguise. F4: three contract-valid remedies whose proposed_action.parameters carry an empty, a whitespace-only and a newline-only key each render a draft the shipped validator refuses, so the write path refuses by name and writes no runbook draft, with a companion assertion that each remedy is itself contract-valid (validate_remedy reports zero problems); the guard is asserted to report the shipped validator's own message ('parameter 0 has no name'), to accept the valid draft (control), to refuse an unparseable draft, and to reach the contract through the one parser and the shipped validate_action rather than a reimplementation. The ACTION WHITELIST STORE root is asserted read from the SHIPPED store location (action.default_actions_dir); the SPEC CORPUS root is an honest literal, asserted as such, because no engine module owns the corpus root - validate.py, plan.py, frontier.py and intent_corpus.py each build root / 'specs' inline - and the store's comment says so plainly rather than claiming both roots are derived. A draft asked to carry a review block is refused by name across four variants, and the renderer returns a draft for review status proposed and nothing for any other review block (control).

The receipt (warp.reconciliation/v1) records what was done from the EXECUTION RECEIPT rather than the remedy's claim about itself, what it proved via the proposal digest RECOMPUTED through the shipped .warp/action_executor.py proposal_digest, and what regression criteria it leaves as the paths and digests of the two AC3 drafts, plus the failure signature, recurrence_of and missing_specification. An execution asked to be recorded with no receipt, or with a receipt whose proposal digest does not match the recomputed one, REFUSES by name. The receipt id is content-addressed from the settlement identity, and the store is append-only with compare-and-swap on THREE outcomes rather than two (the round-1 defect F3, closed): a replay returns the existing receipt and appends no second record and no second event; a conflicting write under an existing id refuses rather than overwriting; and a record that EXISTS but cannot be read or parsed into a mapping is a CONFLICT rather than an absence, refused by name (reconciliation_receipt_unreadable). Round 1 swallowed OSError and ValueError in _get and returned None, so a crash-truncated receipt read as ABSENT, was overwritten, and appended a SECOND incident.closed for one incident - the exact corruption the spec's Notes single out, since a duplicated incident.closed silently corrupts every WARP-1210 measure. Absence and corruption are now different answers: None means nothing is recorded, and the UNREADABLE sentinel (deliberately neither None nor a mapping, so no caller can read fields off a corrupt record. HONEST CORRECTION (round-2 review): the sentinel is compared by OBJECT IDENTITY, so a caller who loads reconciliation_store.py itself gets a different sentinel object and the pass's closed-replay branch treats a corrupt receipt as a settled record. The WRITE path is immune (settle returns the string outcome), so the overwrite and the duplicate event this criterion is about stay closed; the identity comparison is recorded as the first item of the follow-up hardening) means a record exists and cannot be read. Settlement appends incident.closed using the vocabulary reused from .warp/incident.py, and .warp/validate.py EVENT_TYPES carries the four incident lifecycle types (the recognition WARP-1201 deliberately deferred to this item).

The honest receipt over a seeded executed lifecycle; the receipt's parameters win over the remedy's when they differ; a receipt recording no parameters yields the honest value none; a receipt recording a refusal is reconciled as refused; an incident with no remedy at all settles with an honest none execution block; both execution-claim refusals by name; a full replay producing zero new records, zero new events and the SAME receipt id; an already-closed incident taking the idempotent replay path; the compare-and-swap conflict refusing by name without overwriting; the content-addressed id; and the drift binding that incident.INCIDENT_EVENT_TYPES is a subset of BOTH events.EVENT_TYPES and validate.EVENT_TYPES so the emitter, the metric source and the gate cannot drift. F3 is proven over a REAL temporary tree with the reviewer's own attack: settle, then corrupt the receipt four ways (crash-truncated JSON, bytes that are not JSON at all, a payload that is not a mapping, a payload that is a list) and re-run - each refuses by name, the corrupt file is NOT overwritten, and the event stream still carries exactly ONE incident.closed. Further assertions prove the store tells absence from corruption (None versus the sentinel), that settle() names the third outcome, that an already-closed incident whose receipt is unreadable refuses too rather than returning a corrupt record as proof it is settled, and the CONTROL that with the receipt restored the very same re-run is an idempotent replay again (the refusal is about corruption, not about replay).

AC4 TEETH on the recognition itself: with the four incident types removed from the recognition set in memory, the SAME emitted incident.closed event is REJECTED as an unknown event type. The gate's recognition is load-bearing, not decoration. Observed live during the selftest run as the line "unknown event type 'incident.closed'" in the output of a temporary fixture stream.

TWELVE guards, TWELVE teeth, each neutralized in memory ALONE in the organ that OWNS it and each observed to turn its own refusing fixture green: T-status (the status gate), T-validation (the missing-validation refusal), T-machine (the machine-actor refusal), T-remedybinding (the unbound-remedy refusal, new), T-digest (the recomputed-digest comparison), T-debt (the open-emergency-debt refusal), T-reviewed (the reviewed-draft refusal), T-draftvalid (the structural-validity refusal, new), T-claim (the unsupported-execution-claim refusal, covering both the no-receipt and digest-mismatch paths under one guard with one home), T-draftpath (the draft path guard, in the store), T-cas (the compare-and-swap conflict check, in the store), T-unreadable (the unreadable-receipt sentinel, in the store, new). Nine live in .warp/incident_reconcile.py and three in .warp/reconciliation_store.py; a store mutation is driven through the REAL pass, because the store is an injected seam, so a mutant store instance is simply passed in. Each mutation target is asserted to appear EXACTLY ONCE in the organ that owns it, so no mutation can silently match nothing and report a false green.

THE FULL MATRIX, which the round-1 evidence did not carry and the reviewer produced by hand: all 144 cells of the 12x12 matrix (every mutation against every guard's refusing fixture) are asserted to be exactly the DIAGONAL - each mutation flips ONLY its own fixture, every other fixture still refuses by its own name, and exactly 12 of the 144 cells are green. The path guard's two SUB-MECHANISMS get their own teeth, honestly outside the matrix: neutralizing the RESOLUTION alone makes a '..' traversal reachable again, and neutralizing the CASE FOLD alone makes a case variant reachable again, each over its own crafted fixture, with both organs sha256-unchanged. assumptions: This manifest describes the HARDENING tree (round 2). Round 1's implementation commit ad65e2a and evidence commit 9d57471 stay in history; the independent adversarial review of round 1 (proof/WARP-1208/verdict.json, verdict fail) named four must-fix defects and seven manifest overstatements, and this manifest is the corrected record. Nothing here should be read as review approval: a SECOND independent adversarial review runs in a distinct fresh context and lands as its own commit.

The four round-1 defects are closed as follows, each structurally rather than by test alone. F1: the draft path guard resolves its target to a real absolute path (traversal collapsed, symlinks followed, relative targets anchored) and compares case-insensitively, and an unresolvable target refuses. F2: the recomputed material binds the remedy's identity and its canonical proposal digest, and a validation that names no remedy while one exists refuses by name. F3: an existing-but-unreadable receipt is a distinct third store outcome refused by name, never an absence. F4: the rendered runbook draft is validated through the shipped action.validate_action inside the write path and refused by name if it does not pass.

THE SEVEN OVERSTATEMENTS the reviewer enumerated are corrected in this manifest rather than defended. (1) 'the forbidden roots are read from the SHIPPED store location rather than hardcoded' - only the whitelist store root is; the spec corpus root is a literal, now stated as such in the manifest, in the store's comment, and in a selftest assertion, because no engine module owns the corpus root. (2) 'the writer REFUSES BY NAME any target inside the action whitelist store' - false in round 1 by traversal, symlink and case; the claim is now stated as refusing any target that RESOLVES inside, with the resolution and case-insensitivity named, and capabilities.yaml carries the same corrected sentence. (3) the append-only claim - now stated as three outcomes including the unreadable-record conflict. (4) structural validity 'against warp.action/v1' stated unconditionally - now stated as ENFORCED through the shipped validator inside the write path, with the refusal named. (5) the WARP-0619 lesson invocation - now stated with what it buys, which is a recomputed digest over material that actually contains the diagnosis and its cited evidence. (6) 'a repository-wide grep for incident_reconcile returns only capabilities.yaml' - it also returns the spec; both are named. (7) 'the declared footprint matches the diff exactly' - now stated with the shape gate's own diff definition and its exclusions, and specs/index.md is declared in the footprint.

The definition of 'diagnosis material' was REJECTED by the round-1 review and is redefined here: the incident's identity and failure fields plus, whenever a remedy exists, the remedy's id and its canonical proposal digest (action_executor.proposal_digest, reused not reimplemented). The alternative the reviewer's finding also permits - hashing the remedy's diagnosis and cited evidence fields directly - was rejected because it would be a SECOND, weaker remedy identity that leaves the rest of the proposal's substance free to change after a human validated, and because reusing the canonical digest makes the human's validation and the executor's confirmation bind the same artifact. A reviewer should judge that choice; the justification is in the module docstring, not only here.

The store extraction is a structural change the reviewer's assumption ruling recommended, not a cosmetic one: .warp/reconciliation_store.py owns the compare-and-swap, the unreadable-record refusal, the draft writes and the path guard, and the pass re-exports its public surface so callers have one front door and there is exactly one definition of each store mechanism and each store-decided refusal name. HONEST RESIDUAL: the pass is 937 of 1000 lines, which is lower than round 1's 995 with four more guards in it but is not comfortable headroom. The next natural seam is the draft RENDERERS (about 185 lines); it was NOT taken here because the renderers depend on the pass's own vocabulary (SETTLED_BY, the draft constants, missing_specification), so splitting them would either duplicate that vocabulary or invert the dependency between the pass and its artifacts. If this organ grows again, that seam - or a shared draft-vocabulary module below both - is the place to cut.

The teeth matrix is exactly the diagonal for the twelve GUARDS. The path guard's two sub-mechanisms (the resolution and the case fold) are proven with their own mutations and their own fixtures but are deliberately NOT matrix rows, because they feed the same refusal decision as the outer path-guard check, which therefore dominates them by construction: neutralizing the outer check also flips their fixtures. That nesting is asserted, not hidden. Reading them as matrix rows would show two off-diagonal cells; reading them as sub-mechanisms of one guard, which is what they are, leaves the guard matrix diagonal.
